description:
## What

Update section references and version stamps in pkix-profiles-cabf and pkix-lint-cabf to match the current CA/B Forum spec layouts. Audit done 2026-05-12; values still match current BR but citations point at wrong section headers due to upstream renumbering (ballot SC65 converted EVGs into RFC 3647 format; comparable reorganizations applied to TLS BR / S/MIME BR / CS BR).

**Substantive policy enforcement is still correct.** Only the labels are stale. This is label hygiene, not a behavior fix.

## Specific changes required

### pkix-profiles-cabf/src/lib.rs

WebPkiProfile (TLS BR 2.2.6):

- §7.1.4.2 (SAN required) -> §7.1.2.7.12 (Subscriber Certificate Subject Alternative Name)
- §7.1.2.7.3 (id-kp-serverAuth) -> §7.1.2.7.10 (Subscriber Certificate Extended Key Usage)
- §7.1.1 (max_path_len = 2) -> needs verification — current §7.1.1 is 'Version number(s).' The path-length is not in a single dedicated section; may need to cite §6.1.2 (CA hierarchy) or §7.1.2.6 (TLS Subordinate CA Certificate Profile) depending on intent. Re-read BR to find correct anchor.
- version() = 'SC-081' is judgment-call. SC-081 is the ballot reference, not doc version. Decide whether to keep as ballot-stamp or bump to '2.2.6'.

SmimeProfile (S/MIME BR 1.0.14):

- §7.3 (id-kp-emailProtection) -> §7.1.2.3(f) (Subscriber certificate extKeyUsage)
- §7.2 (max_path_len = 1) -> §7.1.2.2 (Subordinate CA certificates)
- version() = '1.0' -> '1.0.14'. Or update to whichever ballot label conveys current state (latest material ballot is SMC016, SHA-1 sunset).
- Note: SMC016 (effective 2026-09-15) adds a CA-side SHA-1 sunset; validator side already prohibits SHA-1 via CABF_SMIME_BR_ALLOWED_ALGS so no enforcement change needed.

CodeSigningProfile (CS BR 3.10.0):

- §7.1.1 (max 1 intermediate) -> not §7.1.1 ('Version number(s)'); needs the correct path-length anchor; possibly §6.1.2 or implicit in §7.1.2.2 (Subordinate CA Certificate). Re-read BR.
- version() = '3.0' -> '3.10.0' or current ballot stamp.

### pkix-lint-cabf/src/cabf_tls_br.rs

Same drift as WebPkiProfile, applied to citation() returns + spec_section_id() returns + rustdoc citations:

- ValidityMaxLint citation §6.3.2 (SC-081) — OK, keep
- Sha1ProhibitedLint citation §7.1.3 — OK, keep
- RsaMinKeySizeLint citation §6.1.5 — OK, keep
- SanRequiredLint citation §7.1.4.2 -> §7.1.2.7.12
- EkuServerAuthLint citation §7.1.2.7.3 -> §7.1.2.7.10
- BcCaFlagLint citation §7.1.2.5 (Technically Constrained TLS Sub CA Profile, wrong subset) -> needs decision: §7.1.2.6 (general TLS Sub CA), §7.1.2.2 (Cross-Cert Sub CA), or umbrella RFC 5280 §4.2.1.9. The lint's applies_to is SubjectKind::IntermediateCa, so the citation should cover the general intermediate CA case, not a specific subset.

Also update the rustdoc table at top of cabf_tls_br.rs file (the one listing each lint with citation), plus the citation strings inside each Lint impl.

## What's NOT in scope

- Updating CABF_TLS_BR_ALLOWED_ALGS / CABF_SMIME_BR_ALLOWED_ALGS / CABF_CS_BR_ALLOWED_ALGS — values are still correct
- Adding new lints from new ballots — the unprincipled-exception clause keeps the surface small
- Adding pkix-profiles-cabf Cross-Certified Subordinate CA Profile coverage — separate scope (PKIX-jbvb for S/MIME sub-profiles; nothing parallel for TLS Cross-Cert today)
- Updating sc081_validity_cap helper — values match SC-081 ballot

## Acceptance

- [ ] All section references in rustdoc / citation() / spec_section_id() match current BR layout
- [ ] Version stamps reflect current ballot or doc version (decide which)
- [ ] divergences.md (or equivalent) in pkix-lint-cabf and pkix-profiles-cabf documenting which BR ballot the crate was last refreshed against and the policy on how often to refresh
- [ ] cargo test passes (no behavior changes; this is label hygiene)
- [ ] CHANGELOG entries flagging citation refresh

## Audit reference

Full citation drift analysis recorded in conversation transcript 2026-05-12 (immediate context: CABF spec refresh commit 3ae0283c brought specs/ to TLS BR 2.2.6 / EVG 2.0.2 / S/MIME BR 1.0.14 / CS BR 3.10.0; crate citations had drifted against the renumbered specs). Root cause: TLS BR ballot SC65 (RFC 3647 format conversion) plus comparable reorganizations in S/MIME BR and CS BR.

## Cross-references

- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5 unprincipled-exception clause — accepts this maintenance burden as the cost of the -cabf crates' existence
- pkix-lint-cabf/src/lib.rs — crate-level rustdoc references CA/B Forum BR URLs (do not need updating; those URLs are stable)
- specs/cabforum-BR.md (TLS BR 2.2.6)
- specs/cabforum-smime-BR.md (S/MIME BR 1.0.14)
- specs/cabforum-code-signing-BR.md (CS BR 3.10.0)
notes:
[2026-05-13 bd-spin scoping pass] Audit shows the unambiguous citation refreshes (§7.1.4.2 → §7.1.2.7.12 SAN, §7.1.2.7.3 → §7.1.2.7.10 EKU) are mechanical and ready to apply. But three items in the bead description require human judgment that an autonomous agent shouldn't make unilaterally:

1. **Path-length anchor**: 'max_path_len = 2' in WebPkiProfile cites §7.1.1, which the bead acknowledges is wrong ('Version number(s)'). My grep of cabforum-BR.md cannot find the '2 non-self-issued intermediates' rule anywhere in the current BR text. The CA hierarchy section (§6.1.2) discusses Root → Subordinate → Subscriber structurally but does not enforce a numeric depth limit. The BR may have dropped this requirement entirely in renumbering, or it may have been a workspace-side assumption from another source (Mozilla root policy?). Three options: (a) cite §6.1.2 with a note that the numeric depth is workspace policy, (b) cite the relevant historical TLS BR section + version where it was last present, (c) drop the max_path_len = 2 enforcement entirely if it's no longer in the BR. Same question applies to CodeSigningProfile and SmimeProfile path-length citations.

2. **Version-stamp format**: bead asks 'decide whether to keep as ballot-stamp (SC-081) or bump to doc-version (2.2.6)'. Workspace convention not established. Suggest mark a stance for all three crates simultaneously to keep them symmetric.

3. **BcCaFlagLint citation**: bead lists three plausible targets (§7.1.2.6, §7.1.2.2, RFC 5280 §4.2.1.9). My read: applies_to=IntermediateCa is broad enough that RFC 5280 §4.2.1.9 is the cleanest umbrella citation — but that turns this lint from CA/B Forum-specific into RFC-conformance, which would imply moving it to pkix-lint. Or pick §7.1.2.6 (general TLS Sub CA) and accept that Cross-Cert Sub CAs covered by §7.1.2.2 share the same rule. Substantive editorial decision.

Recommend filing 3 sub-beads (one per item) for human decision, then a follow-up bead can do the mechanical citation refresh once the three judgment calls are made. Mechanical work is small once the calls are made; current bead conflates mechanical + judgment.

Not claiming or partially executing this bead — the value of a citation refresh is that it leaves the codebase consistent; partial execution makes it worse.
[2026-05-13 decisions recorded by Mark]

Three judgment calls bd-spin surfaced are resolved. All on recommended path.

**D1 — Path-length enforcement: DROP ENTIRELY.**

Research confirmed: no current CA/B Forum BR (TLS BR 2.2.6, S/MIME BR 1.0.14, CS BR 3.10.0) caps chain depth. Each spec only constrains pathLenConstraint extension presence/value on individual cert types in their basicConstraints tables (§7.1.2.10.4, §7.1.2.1.4, §7.1.2.7.8 in TLS BR; analogous sections in others). The workspace's max_path_len = 2 / 1 was workspace-added defense, not BR requirement.

Action: remove `max_path_len` field initialization from WebPkiProfile, SmimeProfile, CodeSigningProfile policy() outputs. Remove the corresponding citations. RFC 5280 §4.2.1.9 pathLenConstraint enforcement (already in pkix-path) handles per-cert constraints unchanged. **Behavior change: chains depth >2 will now pass WebPkiProfile validation that previously failed.** CHANGELOG entry MUST call this out.

**D2 — BasicConstraints cA=TRUE citation: §7.1.2.10.4 'CA Certificate Basic Constraints'.**

Umbrella section. Every specific Sub CA profile in §7.1.2.2/.3/.4/.5/.6 explicitly cross-references it. Correct for BcCaFlagLint's applies_to: IntermediateCa scope.

Action: update `BcCaFlagLint::citation()` and `spec_section_id()` in pkix-lint-cabf/src/cabf_tls_br.rs to point at §7.1.2.10.4. Update rustdoc table at top of file.

**D3 — Version-stamp convention: dotted spec version.**

Matches each spec's own subtitle. Comparable across refreshes without ballot lookup. Coarse-grained, matches workspace wholesale-refresh stance for the -cabf crates.

Action: update `WebPkiProfile::version()` → `"2.2.6"`, `SmimeProfile::version()` → `"1.0.14"`, `CodeSigningProfile::version()` → `"3.10.0"`. Keep the version() accessor (no API change), update rustdoc.

**D4 (surfaced) — version() accessor: keep as-is.**

Public API stays. Documented as advisory; consumers may log/audit.

## Implementation cascade (one actionable bead from here)

1. **pkix-profiles-cabf/src/lib.rs**:
   - WebPkiProfile.policy(): remove max_path_len = Some(2) initialization
   - SmimeProfile.policy(): remove max_path_len = Some(1) initialization
   - CodeSigningProfile.policy(): remove max_path_len = Some(1) initialization
   - WebPkiProfile.version() → "2.2.6"
   - SmimeProfile.version() → "1.0.14"
   - CodeSigningProfile.version() → "3.10.0"
   - SAN section citation §7.1.4.2 → §7.1.2.7.12 (Subscriber Certificate Subject Alternative Name)
   - EKU section citation §7.1.2.7.3 → §7.1.2.7.10 (Subscriber Certificate Extended Key Usage)
   - Remove §7.1.1 / §7.2 / §7.1.1 path-length citations (no replacement)
   - S/MIME: emailProtection citation §7.3 → §7.1.2.3(f)
   - Update rustdoc throughout

2. **pkix-lint-cabf/src/cabf_tls_br.rs**:
   - SanRequiredLint citation §7.1.4.2 → §7.1.2.7.12
   - EkuServerAuthLint citation §7.1.2.7.3 → §7.1.2.7.10
   - BcCaFlagLint citation §7.1.2.5 → §7.1.2.10.4
   - Update rustdoc table at top of file
   - Other citations (§6.3.2, §7.1.3, §6.1.5) already correct, no change

3. **CHANGELOG** entries on pkix-profiles-cabf and pkix-lint-cabf:
   - Path-length enforcement removed from CABF profiles (behavior change: chains deeper than 2 will now pass; this matches the BR's actual text)
   - Citation refresh against current BR layouts
   - Version stamps updated to current spec versions
   - No new functionality, no API removal (just behavior/citation/version changes)

4. **divergences.md** (new file) on pkix-profiles-cabf and pkix-lint-cabf:
   - Documents that these crates are wholesale snapshots, not ballot-tracking
   - Records last-refreshed-against date and BR version
   - References AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5 unprincipled-exception clause

5. **Test impact audit** — does any test in pkix-profiles-cabf or pkix-difftest rely on the dropped max_path_len behavior? Audit before merging.

human label removed; bead is actionable for autonomous loop.
title: Refresh CABF crate citations against current spec layout (TLS BR 2.2.6 / S/MIME BR 1.0.14 / CS BR 3.10.0)
